2.summary: 1 Platoon of A Company, 5 RAR, made contact with five enemy soldiers moving south. The result was not known.

52.summary: 1 ATF's artillery fired on enemy mortar positions at Phuoc Long, a fortified Viet Cong village where the positions were well dug in and linked by tunnels. The Viet Cong had fired about 20 rounds.

66.summary: D Company, 5 RAR, was sweeping the north-east of Hoa Long for enemy mortar positions when its force came under light mortar fire. One Australian was killed and three wounded, from D and E Platoon, 1 APC Squadron and 1 Field Squadron. Radar placed the mortars at Long Phuoc village, and artillery fired on them with unknown results.

105.summary: The SAS squadron came under machine-gun and rifle fire on its left flank during the night. A standing patrol then saw four or five enemy in a paddy field 120 metres away, but they disappeared before they could be fired on.

180.summary: C Company, 6 RAR, was part of a two-company cordon, with two other companies driving the enemy towards it, when it met an estimated Viet Cong company. As the enemy withdrew, covered by a rearguard of about 15, C Company called in artillery; two Australians were wounded, which the battalion's commander put down to a platoon mistaking its own position rather than to the artillery. The company then came under mortar fire and fought several small-arms clashes, hitting about four enemy, and found a large bunker system nearby. Four enemy bodies killed by artillery were recovered over the following days.

181.summary: B Company, 6 RAR, was manning a cut-off line on a track in a battalion cordon when its sentries opened fire on two groups of Viet Cong, probably most of a company. 6 Platoon brought artillery down on the enemy, but when it rose to clear the area it was hit by rifle and mortar fire, and one Australian shell fell short into the company's position, killing two and wounding several. By the time the enemy withdrew the company had two killed and twelve wounded; at least six enemy were killed and about fifteen wounded. The commanders afterwards debated whether the troops' strict fire discipline had let the enemy's fire go unanswered for too long.

218.summary: The Viet Cong shelled the Task Force's artillery lines at Nui Dat with about 66 rounds from 82 mm mortars and what was thought to be a 70 mm howitzer, killing one Australian and wounding 24. The artillery returned fire within seven minutes. A patrol from B Company, 6 RAR, later found the firing positions, with signs of a hurried departure, blood trails and carts used to take bodies away. This was the night before the Battle of Long Tan.

220.summary: The Battle of Long Tan. D Company, 6 RAR, 108 strong, was following fresh tracks east of Nui Dat when 11 Platoon met a few Viet Cong and then a much larger force. From about 5.30 pm the company was attacked by at least a company, later found to be far more, under heavy machine-gun and mortar fire in heavy rain, and held on until A Company arrived in armoured personnel carriers after 7 pm. Close artillery fire broke up many of the attacks; low cloud ruled out air strikes, and helicopters flew in ammunition and took out the wounded. Seventeen Australians were killed and nineteen wounded; 245 enemy were recorded killed. The company commander afterwards reported that the M60 machine-guns jammed in the mud and that the men needed to carry more ammunition.

222.summary: During the Battle of Long Tan, A Company, 6 RAR, rode out from Nui Dat in the armoured personnel carriers of 3 Troop, 1 APC Squadron, to relieve D Company. On the way it clashed with the support company of the D445 Battalion, causing about 15 casualties, and then with two companies of the 275th Regiment, causing about 45 more, before joining D Company as the enemy withdrew. Four Australians were wounded.

368.summary: A command-detonated mine exploded against D Company, 6 RAR, killing one Australian and wounding ten, with three civilians also wounded. About half the casualties, including the man killed, were caused by an Australian Claymore mine carried by an NCO, which went off in the blast. The record also notes evidence that a Vietnamese woman who ran to the scene was wounded or killed by soldiers who mistook her for an enemy.

445.summary: 6 RAR was being flown in by helicopter to cut off enemy forces retreating from an attack on Phuoc Hai. 2 Platoon, A Company, pushing into the jungle to secure the landing zone, came under sniper fire and then ran into a Viet Cong company dug into bunkers with overhead cover. Six Australians were wounded, five of them by an automatic weapon; three to six enemy were killed. The platoon withdrew 150 metres.

447.summary: Operation Bribie. After A Company, 6 RAR, found a Viet Cong company and its heavy weapons company dug into bunkers, B Company was ordered to assault the position. It was pinned down by fire from all sides, including heavy machine-guns, Claymore mines and mortars; four air strikes were called in, and carriers of 2 Troop, A Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, went in to bring out the wounded, one being disabled by recoilless-rifle fire. After four hours both companies withdrew into the battalion's night position, and the enemy left during the night. Eight Australians were killed and 21 wounded; about 50 enemy were recorded killed. The battalion's commander said that tanks could have taken the position with little difficulty.

452.summary: B Company, 5 RAR, was moving by armoured personnel carrier towards the Long Hai Hills for a Task Force attack when the leading carrier hit a powerful mine, killing two cavalrymen and two infantrymen and badly wounding the rest aboard. Men who ran to help the wounded set off more anti-personnel mines, killing or wounding most of the medics and company headquarters, until engineers ordered everyone to keep still while they cleared the area. Nine Australians were killed and 26 wounded, and Operation Renmark was cancelled.

490.summary: 5 Platoon, B Company, 7 RAR, opened fire when the enemy probed its defences. There were no known casualties.

526.summary: While laying the barrier minefield, a member of a mine-arming party from 7 RAR's assault pioneers set off an M16 mine, killing one sapper of 1 Field Squadron and wounding two.

541.summary: A sentry of B Company, 2 RAR, saw an enemy soldier at the perimeter wire and threw a grenade. There were no enemy casualties.

568.summary: 3 Troop's position at Duc Thanh was shelled by 60 mm mortars. Artillery at Nui Dat returned fire and silenced them. No carriers were damaged, and four men were slightly wounded.

586.summary: Operation Ballarat, in the Hat Dich area. A Company, 7 RAR, had been inserted quietly to ambush trails to enemy camps, and its 2 Platoon killed two enemy who walked into a hasty ambush. Sent along the track after the rest of the enemy squad, the platoon ran into heavy automatic fire from a defended position held by a company of the 274th Regiment's 3rd Battalion, covering the withdrawal of its battalion from a camp nearby. The whole company was committed, supported by air strikes and by 106 Field Battery and a US battery, until the enemy withdrew after about four hours. Six Australians were killed and about twenty wounded; an estimated 15 enemy were killed and 25 wounded by the company, and many more by the artillery and air strikes.

672.summary: 2 Platoon, A Company, 2 RAR, was in ambush on a track about a kilometre north of Long Tan, well inside the prohibited zone, when 16 Vietnamese came along it. The machine-gunner took a raised carrying pole for a weapon and opened fire, and the rest of the ambush joined in; the commander stopped the firing when he heard a woman's voice. They were all unarmed civilians: four were killed, six wounded and captured, and three more taken prisoner.

697.summary: Several enemy got through the defensive perimeter of 108 Field Battery and set up four Claymore mines aimed at its sleeping quarters. Two were fired, killing one gunner; the other two did not go off. Most of the battery was on duty at the time, or the casualties would have been far higher.

721.summary: A command-detonated Claymore mine was fired into 2 Platoon, A Company, 7 RAR's base from outside the perimeter, probably aimed at the sound of its radio, killing two Australians and wounding six. Sweeping the area, the platoon killed two Viet Cong and captured two rifles. The company commander noted that a helicopter visit an hour earlier may have given the position away, and that the men had run to the wounded without waiting for a sweep, risking a second mine.

737.summary: Acting on SAS intelligence, D Company, 7 RAR, assaulted an occupied Viet Cong base camp while B Company waited in ambush on the escape routes. 10 and 12 Platoons took several bunkers, but when they reached the centre of the camp the enemy, using communication trenches, came round behind them and attacked from three sides, firing rocket-propelled grenades into the tree canopy to rain shrapnel on the Australians. Close quarters ruled out artillery and helicopter gunships, and grenade launchers and a machine-gun failed. The fighting, in heavy rain, died away at nightfall; two Australians were shot dead and about 21 wounded by shrapnel, several of whom stayed on duty. The camp had been used by the D445 Battalion and the Chau Duc district company.

746.summary: A 12-man patrol of 2 Platoon, A Company, 2 RAR, was hit by a command-detonated mine, and the enemy opened fire. The patrol returned fire and called in artillery. Two Australians were killed and eight wounded.

751.summary: 106 Field Battery saw two people moving in front of its position and fired Claymore mines. A search of the area found nothing.

753.summary: 12 Platoon, D Company, 2 RAR, ambushed six Viet Cong, killing four and wounding one, and captured three weapons. A tracking team followed a blood trail until it was lost at a river, and 108 Field Battery fired on likely escape routes. Papers on one of the dead showed he was the commander of the Xuyen Moc district platoon.

768.summary: 106 Field Battery, supporting Operation Forrest from Fire Support Base Bravo, was hit by a single round from outside the perimeter, possibly a grenade or a mortar bomb. One Australian died of wounds, and an investigation began.

774.summary: A long-range patrol of 1 SAS Squadron ambushed seven Viet Cong, five men and two women, dressed in mixed clothing and carrying a large amount of food. All seven were killed and three weapons captured.

780.summary: The advance party of 3 RAR on patrol saw two Viet Cong in black, one carrying two weapons and the other a sack, 100 to 150 metres away. They fled, and a tracking team lost their trail. There were no casualties.

791.summary: 12 Platoon, D Company, 7 RAR, found an enemy camp and met two enemy, who fled; sweeping the area, it met and killed another. 106 Field Battery probably fired in support.

794.summary: 1 Platoon, A Company, 7 RAR, ambushed three enemy with two Claymore mines, machine-guns and rifles, killing two at once and the third, wounded, in the sweep that followed. Three SKS rifles were captured, and 106 Field Battery fired in support.

847.summary: 5 Platoon, B Company, 2 RAR, ran into 15 to 20 enemy in a camp and called in artillery and mortars in a heavy fight. One Australian was killed, one died of wounds and one was wounded; the enemy left two bodies, blood trails and drag marks.

852.summary: 9 Platoon, C Company, 2 RAR, assaulted an enemy camp and had only just occupied its horseshoe-shaped defences when 20 or more enemy of the 274th Regiment and the Trang Bom district unit counter-attacked. The fight went on for three hours, the enemy attacking seven times with heavy machine-guns, and helicopter gunships, air strikes and artillery were called in. Two Australians were killed; two enemy were killed and more wounded, and the camp yielded weapons, packs and a large quantity of rice and food.

856.summary: Following up its bunker contact of the day before, C Company, 2 RAR, was fired on from a bunker, which it found and grenaded along with at least one more. It then came under fire from three sides and from snipers, with one platoon pinned down so that every movement drew fire, and two men were wounded. Artillery was fired, the wounded were evacuated, and the company was able to disengage; V Company, sent to help, arrived later over hard going. One enemy body and four blood trails were found, and two rifles and 700 pounds of food captured.

860.summary: 10 Platoon, D Company, 7 RAR, unknowingly approached an enemy camp held by more than a company, and the forward section was hit as it crossed a deep gully. With the platoon nearly out of ammunition and under grenade-launcher and mortar fire, helicopter gunships struck the enemy only 30 metres away, and the rest of the company came up, assaulted both flanks and cleared the camp as the enemy withdrew in disorder. One Australian was killed and ten wounded, mostly by grenades and rockets. The enemy, of the C238 Battalion, had been massing for an attack on Long Binh.

875.summary: 2 Platoon, A Company, 7 RAR, was holding an ambush when a large body of enemy approached. Claymores and machine-guns killed four of the first five into the killing ground, but 20 or more enemy fought back hard with rifles, machine-guns and rocket-propelled grenades. One Australian, the platoon's medic, died of his wounds and seven were wounded, many by rocket shrapnel; eight enemy were killed.

895.summary: A platoon made contact at 15 metres on the edge of an enemy camp, taking three casualties, and called in artillery and mortars. B Company, 2 RAR, assaulted the camp that afternoon but was pinned down by a machine-gun and rocket-propelled grenades, with enemy appearing from one bunker as soon as another was cleared. V Company, gunships and an air strike were sent to help, and after the wounded were evacuated B Company pulled back 300 metres from a bunker system much larger than first thought. Five Australians were wounded and four enemy killed.

903.summary: During the Tet Offensive a Viet Cong battalion seized much of Ba Ria, a town of 15,000, and the province headquarters asked 1 ATF for help. A Company, 3 RAR, less a platoon, with nine armoured personnel carriers of 3 Troop, A Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, was rushed in by carrier to protect the US compound and other key buildings, and fought through a town full of uncleared houses, infiltrators and rocket teams. One Australian was killed and nineteen wounded; 42 enemy were recorded killed.

906.summary: The battle for Trang Bom, during the Tet Offensive. D Company, 2 RAR, carried in armoured personnel carriers of A Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, was sent with South Vietnamese forces to drive a Viet Cong force out of the village. Heavy rocket and automatic fire kept them out at first; helicopter gunships attacked, and the advance was slowed by the need to move civilians still in their homes to the market place. The enemy withdrew under cover of smoke from burning houses, came back that night, and was driven out again the next day with carrier and artillery support. Across the two days 19 enemy were recorded killed, most by artillery and carriers; no Australians were lost, but six civilians were killed by artillery.

966.summary: After air strikes and gunships had hit an enemy camp, C Company, 7 RAR, went in by a wide flanking move. The camp seemed deserted until Viet Cong in four large, well-hidden bunkers opened fire at ten metres, pinning the leading sections in crossfire; anti-tank rockets had little effect on the bunkers. The company pulled back 15 metres and brought artillery, mortars and a gunship strike in very close, after which the enemy withdrew in good order. Fourteen Australians were wounded, none seriously, six staying on duty overnight; three enemy were killed and five wounded, and the company commander thought more.

977.summary: 5 Platoon, B Company, 3 RAR, was covering 4 Platoon's search for a missing South Vietnamese battalion commander at Long Dien when its forward sections came under heavy fire from a Viet Cong platoon. Three Australians were killed and four wounded, and nine Viet Cong were killed. The enemy took a radio from an Australian signaller, and may have taken weapons from the casualties.

1005.summary: Fire Support Base Anderson was attacked at night by at least a company and a mortar platoon. After an accurate bombardment of mortar bombs and rockets, the enemy assaulted in waves through the rear of a US battery and 3 RAR's mortar lines, breaking into the perimeter; the machine-guns of 1 Troop, A Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment's carriers, the US battery and mortar fire drove them back, and further probes failed at the wire. Four enemy bodies were found, with signs of many more casualties. Seven Australians were killed and about 24 wounded, and one American killed; four sappers of 1 Field Squadron died when a mortar bomb hit their standing patrol.

1014.summary: C Company, 7 RAR, saw torches 800 metres from its position. 106 Field Battery and mortars fired on them, and the lights went out.

1033.summary: B Company, 2 RAR, took the Dinh Co hill in the north-west of the Long Hai Hills. An engineer set off a booby trap in the temple, killing himself and wounding 13 others. The company commander reported the area thick with mines and booby traps, and that the enemy were placing them at places Westerners were likely to visit.

1042.summary: A tank of C Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, was hit by a rocket-propelled grenade, damaging the tank and wounding one Australian. Artillery fired on the area with unknown results.

1051.summary: The perimeter defence of 2 Platoon, W Company, 2 RAR, ambushed five enemy, killing three and capturing one; the company caught the last man at dawn. Four weapons were captured, and 108 Field Battery and a US battery fired in support.

1090.summary: A 1 ATF long-range patrol of 2 SAS Squadron set a mine ambush of Claymores and explosives, which went off under a tractor and trailer carrying ammunition, weapons and equipment. Fifteen Viet Cong bodies were counted, and a defector from the unit later said 21 had died; a recoilless rifle was captured and the tractor destroyed. Helicopter gunships attacked the area, setting off secondary explosions, and the patrol was extracted.

1164.summary: A 1 ATF long-range patrol of 2 SAS Squadron was in ambush when eight enemy came in two groups of four. Claymores wiped out the second group, and the patrol killed most of the first, six or seven in all. As it withdrew it was fired on by four more enemy with a machine-gun, and it was extracted.

1183.summary: A 19-man SAS patrol sent to ambush the recently abandoned Fire Support Base Dyke split up to reach a group of enemy it had seen. The main party then came on four more at seven metres and killed all four with rifles and grenade launchers, before attacking the other group.

1233.summary: Fire Support Base Coral, north-east of Saigon, was attacked by an estimated battalion with very heavy and accurate mortar fire, rockets and a ground assault. The enemy overran a 105 mm gun position and 1 RAR's mortar platoon, and were only driven out by dawn, with the support of a gunship aircraft and helicopter gunships; 1 RAR's rifle companies were out in ambush positions one or two kilometres away. Nine Australians were killed and 28 wounded; 55 North Vietnamese were counted dead and one captured.

1255.summary: A Viet Cong group broke contact with 2 Platoon, A Company, 1 RAR, when a gunship arrived. Driven by armoured personnel carriers, those who withdrew north ran into 7 Platoon, C Company's ambush and fought back. One Australian was killed and two wounded; seven Viet Cong were killed, one wounded man captured, and weapons taken.

1272.summary: Fire Support Base Coral was attacked a second time by an estimated regiment: heavy mortar and rocket fire, then a ground assault. It was beaten off with the help of a gunship aircraft, helicopter gunships and an air strike on an enemy anti-aircraft gun. Seven Australians were killed and about 19 wounded, and two Americans wounded; 37 North Vietnamese were counted dead and one captured. Later intelligence assessed that only 100 of the 790 attackers came through unhurt.

1306.summary: About 30 mortar rounds were fired at Fire Support Base Coral but landed outside the perimeter. There was no damage and there were no casualties.

1323.summary: The 165th North Vietnamese Regiment attacked Fire Support Base Balmoral, held by 3 RAR with tanks and carriers: heavy mortar fire, followed by a ground attack by about a company, supported by rockets and machine-guns, from an estimated battalion group. Three Australians were killed and sixteen wounded; six enemy were recorded killed.

1324.summary: To draw attention from the attack on Balmoral, the enemy fired on Fire Support Base Coral for 30 minutes with about 60 mortar bombs and 20 recoilless-rifle rounds. One Australian was killed and two wounded; enemy casualties were not known.

1325.summary: Tanks of C Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, and D Company, 1 RAR, attacked a bunker system near Fire Support Base Coral that had been found the day before. The infantry protected the tanks while they cleared the jungle with canister rounds and blew up or crushed the bunkers; the infantry also used flamethrowers, and rocket-propelled grenades had no effect on the tanks. By dusk 14 to 18 bunkers had been destroyed without Australian loss, and at least seven enemy killed, with more buried in their bunkers.

1330.summary: The North Vietnamese renewed their attack on Fire Support Base Balmoral with a heavy mortar and rocket bombardment and a ground attack by two battalions of the 165th Regiment. The attack broke up on the wire under artillery and helicopter gunship fire. One Australian was killed and six to eight wounded; about 47 to 55 enemy were killed and six captured.

1333.summary: On a reconnaissance in force near Coral, C Company, 1 RAR, was pinned down by heavy mortar, machine-gun and rocket fire from a bunker system, at ranges of 10 to 15 metres, too close for gunships and artillery to help much, and carriers could not get through the jungle. Two tanks arrived from Coral and an assault destroyed eight bunkers; a carrier was hit by a rocket while taking out the wounded. The company then broke contact for air strikes. One Australian was killed and seven wounded; 24 enemy were killed and more probably killed, and five bodies were found when the company returned days later.

1351.summary: 4 Platoon, B Company, set an ambush 50 metres from a track behind a paddy bund, as close as it could get under cover. The machine-gunner let a party of six enemy right into the ambush before opening fire, setting off four Claymores; one enemy was killed and the rest dropped into a creek and escaped. The platoon had arrived late and had no time to site its Claymores well, and the company commander noted that any patrol leaving in daylight was liable to be reported to the Viet Cong by locals.

1357.summary: The record gives no account of this SAS patrol's contact beyond the patrol commander's name; eight enemy were recorded killed.

1360.summary: A 1 ATF long-range patrol of 2 SAS Squadron made contact with an estimated 15 enemy, killing six and possibly two more. There were no Australian casualties, and the patrol was extracted.

1385.summary: A six-man 1 ATF long-range patrol of 2 SAS Squadron engaged more than 25 enemy in khaki and green, armed with a machine-gun and rifles, moving north. Thirteen enemy were killed, and possibly more; there were no Australian casualties, though a grenade launcher was damaged.

1441.summary: The land-clearing team of 1 Field Squadron was working around the Nui Thi Vai and Nui Dinh mountains when two enemy fired a rocket-propelled grenade and rifles at a D8 bulldozer, setting it alight and wounding the driver in the head, chest and legs. The engineers could not put the fire out, so pushed the bulldozer into a cutting and buried it; it was recovered to Nui Dat the next day.

1503.summary: About 100 enemy, of the D445 Battalion, attacked Long Dien with recoilless rifles, rocket-propelled grenades and automatic weapons. B and C Companies of 1 RAR, with tanks of C Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, carriers and helicopter gunships, fought a company-sized force in the town and another group on Route 23, in contacts that went on all day. About eleven Australians were wounded, most of C Company's by a 60 mm mortar; 29 to 40 enemy were recorded killed.

1534.summary: 7 Platoon, C Company, 4 RAR, found what looked like an abandoned bunker system of about 20 interlocking bunkers in thick jungle, and quickly organised a two-section assault. The first bunkers were cleared, but halfway in both sections came under very disciplined rifle fire, and the casualties came in clearing three main bunkers. Two Australians were killed, one died of wounds and six were wounded; two enemy were killed and rice, packs, medical kits and documents captured. The platoon concluded it should have reconnoitred the bunkers more carefully before attacking.

1569.summary: 9 Platoon, C Company, 3 RAR, coming down a hill, met about 20 enemy coming up. The enemy fired rifles and rocket-propelled grenades into the trees, causing splinter wounds; a dog handler and the forward scout were evacuated. Six enemy were possibly killed.

1605.summary: A 1 ATF long-range patrol of 2 SAS Squadron ambushed three ox-carts and eight enemy on a track, killing all eight. Fired on by six to eight more enemy, it called in helicopter gunships, saw six more ox-carts on the track, and was extracted.

1616.summary: 12 Platoon, D Company, 4 RAR, was working through an area full of enemy camps. Its commander, leading a small group along a side track, was seen by enemy in a hidden camp 35 metres away, who set off two mines, one a mortar shell and the other a Claymore, threw a grenade and opened fire. Two Australians were killed and six wounded, all by the mines and grenade; the platoon attacked and swept the camp, but the enemy had gone.

1624.summary: A platoon of B Company, 3 RAR, had covered 200 metres of the Firestone Trail with six Claymores when more than 80 enemy began filing past. The three-man killing party fired the Claymores, one of which failed, and withdrew to the rest of the platoon while artillery was brought down around the killing ground. A sweep the next morning found two bodies and eleven drag marks.

1652.summary: 2 Platoon, A Company, 3 RAR, in ambush near its company base, shot an enemy soldier, and ten minutes later was attacked by at least a platoon with rocket-propelled grenades and machine-guns that began to work round its flank. A rocket hit a machine-gun team, and two Australians died of wounds; six were wounded. 1 Platoon covered 2 Platoon's withdrawal under artillery and very accurate helicopter gunship fire, and after further contacts around the company base the company broke contact. Seven enemy were killed and up to nine more possibly killed.

1657.summary: A 1 ATF long-range patrol of 2 SAS Squadron made contact with seven enemy, killing all seven and capturing four rifles. One Australian was wounded.

1844.summary: A 28-man platoon of C Company, 4 RAR, was sent to find 100 to 200 enemy seen from the air. Half went forward to reconnoitre along a paddy field while the rest waited with three armoured personnel carriers as a reaction force; crossing a tree line, the forward group was hit by a command-detonated Claymore. The reaction force came straight down the paddy, fired on the area and brought the group out, and mortars were fired. One Australian was killed and five wounded.

1900.summary: 3 Platoon, A Company, 9 RAR, sweeping an area, came under fire from a large bunker system with heavy and light machine-guns, rocket-propelled grenades and Claymores. The fight drew in 2 Platoon and lasted three and a half hours, until contact was broken at dusk with the help of artillery, mortars and helicopter gunships. One Australian was killed and six wounded; ten enemy were killed.

1935.summary: 2 Platoon, A Company, 9 RAR, was engaged from the rear by about ten enemy in black and green, who withdrew. Two enemy were killed and three wounded, and rifles and seven packs of rice captured; one Australian was shot in the stomach and two others slightly hurt.

1943.summary: A Company, 9 RAR, was packing up its Claymores to leave its night position when three rocket-propelled grenades were fired at it; one landed among a section of 2 Platoon gathered for orders. Three Australians were killed and five wounded. The platoon returned fire and called in artillery and gunships, and the lesson drawn was not to stand around in groups.

2009.summary: 5 Platoon, B Company, 4 RAR, fired a Claymore at several enemy moving round its perimeter, wounding one, who moaned through the night. The enemy made several attempts to rescue him, firing bursts into the perimeter, and were answered with grenade launchers and rifles. In the morning a body and a rifle were found, with two more blood trails.

2016.summary: 5 Platoon, B Company, 9 RAR, ambushed a creek crossing at first light as about 20 enemy came in quietly and well spread out. Claymores and rifle fire killed three, three more were killed as the rest tried to escape, and artillery and mortars hit the escape routes; six enemy were killed and more later found dead of shrapnel wounds. The platoon commander credited the success to concealment and fire discipline, and to using all its firepower once the ambush was sprung.

2038.summary: D Company, 9 RAR, moving west, ran into a bunker system of 21 bunkers that was bigger than it first thought. 11 Platoon was hit by rocket-propelled grenades, and when the medical helicopter came in, 12 Platoon was fired on by heavy machine-guns and rockets and the helicopter was driven off; the company withdrew while artillery, air strikes and gunships hit the camp, and found it empty the next day. One Australian was killed and five wounded; four enemy bodies were found. The company commander warned against being drawn into a bunker fight without heavy support, and noted how patiently the enemy held fire until a helicopter was hovering.

2059.summary: 8 Platoon, C Company, 9 RAR, entering a gully, fired on an enemy soldier and found itself facing at least a platoon in a bunker system, under rifle and rocket fire. The company commander brought 9 Platoon round the north flank and used artillery to block the south, but 9 Platoon was also hit and pulled back to let the artillery work on the bunkers. After five hours, gunships covered the company's withdrawal and the area was shelled; the bunkers were destroyed the next day after the enemy had gone. Five Australians were wounded and six enemy killed; the enemy's fire, aimed about a metre above the ground, was noted as very well controlled.

2061.summary: Acting on an informant's information, 10 Platoon, D Company, 4 RAR, ambushed four or five boats carrying 12 to 15 enemy. Two boats were sunk and another drifted downstream; the enemy fired back from the south bank, and artillery hit their escape routes. Six enemy were killed.

2064.summary: 1 Troop, B Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, and B Company, 4 RAR, were fired on from bunkers, and attacked them into rocket-propelled grenades, machine-guns and Claymore mines, with air strikes and gunships in support. One tank was badly damaged by four or five rockets. Two Australians were killed and eight wounded, B Company's mostly by Claymores and the tanks' by rockets; W Company joined, and both companies pulled back for heavy artillery and to be resupplied with ammunition. Six enemy were killed.

2078.summary: D Company, 9 RAR, saw rockets being fired from about 600 metres away. Artillery and the mortar platoon fired on the launch site, and shouting and running were heard. A patrol the next morning found seven enemy dead, six makeshift launchers and nine rockets, and more bodies were found in the area in the following days, fifteen in all.

2135.summary: Three Australians and 22 South Vietnamese Regional Force soldiers set an ambush in the paddy fields 150 metres from the tree line of Dat Do. Within 15 minutes the enemy opened fire from the trees with machine-guns, rifles and rockets, pinning the patrol behind the paddy bunds, and several were killed as it tried to withdraw, among them an Australian corporal; the enemy then advanced by fire and movement. Mortar fire from 4 RAR at the Horseshoe stopped them, and they withdrew leaving one dead. The platoon had ambushed from the same place too often, and the enemy had learned its habits.

2162.summary: A Company, 5 RAR, with A Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, was escorting a convoy of trucks up Route 15 in Bien Hoa when two US lorries hit mines 50 metres apart. About 20 Australians were wounded, half of whom stayed on duty, and two Americans.

2208.summary: 11 Platoon, D Company, 5 RAR, was spread along its objective when a platoon of enemy in a bunker system opened fire on all of it at once, leaving the commander no reserve to extract it. Claymores, heavy rifle fire and rocket-propelled grenades caused heavy casualties. 12 Platoon, helicopter gunships and air strikes came in, the artillery achieving little, and after four hours 11 Platoon got clear with its wounded. Two Australians were killed and seven wounded; four enemy bodies were later found in fresh graves.

2227.summary: 12 Platoon, D Company, 9 RAR, came on a latrine and was fired on from an enemy platoon's bunker system, with snipers, a Claymore and rocket-propelled grenades, along a 200-metre front with good fire lanes. It withdrew by fire and movement under gunship, artillery and mortar cover, and the whole company then cleared 25 bunkers of a larger system by evening. One Australian died of wounds and six were wounded; one enemy sniper was shot out of a tree. The platoon noticed the enemy's fire followed its machine-guns, and suggested moving them during a long fight.

2241.summary: 4 RAR's Anti-Tank Platoon, in ambush at night, fired Claymores and machine-guns at enemy movement, lighting the area with hand flares, artillery and mortars. When moaning and movement were heard again, it fired grenades and machine-guns once more. The sweep at first light found seven bodies, blood trails, a drag mark and six rifles.

2385.summary: A tank of B Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, set off a mine on a track south-east of Long Dien, an 80-pound Chinese TNT charge. One Australian was killed and one wounded, and the tank could not move under its own power.

2424.summary: Two bulldozers of 1 Field Squadron set off three M16 mines at the edge of a village south-east of Long Dien. Three Australians were wounded, including a driver and a soldier walking behind, and the bulldozers were slightly damaged.

2443.summary: Tanks of B Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, and D and E Platoon engaged about twenty enemy. One enemy was killed and six wounded, and two rifles, 2,000 rounds of ammunition and two anti-tank grenades were captured.

2492.summary: Fire Support Base Thrust, 9 RAR's headquarters, was hit by 25 to 30 mortar bombs. The enemy fired while the base's own guns were firing, which made their mortar hard to locate; it was found by a patrol the next day. One Australian was killed and six or seven wounded.

2496.summary: The Battle of Binh Ba. B and D Companies of 5 RAR, with tanks of B Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, carriers of B Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, and local Regional and Popular Force troops, fought an estimated 90 enemy in the village of Binh Ba from late morning until evening. One Australian was killed and eight to ten wounded, and two Centurion tanks were damaged; 27 enemy were counted dead, more were recorded later, and two were captured.

2509.summary: A company of the 33rd North Vietnamese Regiment attacked Duc Trung and overwhelmed its local defence platoon. B Company, 5 RAR, was sent to retake it: artillery fire was brought within 20 metres of the houses, helicopter gunships attacked the north and west of the village, and B Company attacked from the south with a troop of tanks. The enemy were routed, and local forces cleared the rest of the village to avoid civilian casualties. Forty enemy were recorded killed.

2541.summary: B Company, 6 RAR, spotted a sentry and sent a platoon and a half to attack what seemed a small camp, their approach hidden by heavy rain. They surprised the enemy and killed the sentry, but the camp proved to be a large bunker system, and the enemy counter-attacked. The whole company was committed, with artillery, helicopter gunships and a gunship aircraft overhead for over an hour; after ten were wounded, the company was ordered to withdraw, hampered by rain and eight to ten snipers in the trees. Two machine-guns failed and radio contact was poor. Nine enemy bodies were found when the company went back in the next day to an empty camp.

2547.summary: A soldier of D Company, 5 RAR, stepped on an M16 mine on the southern edge of Dat Do; the mine jumped two metres before exploding. Three Australians were killed and 24 wounded. Another mine, laid only in the last few days, was found nearby, and the report notes the district chief had been told three days earlier that the company would be there.

2550.summary: 10 Platoon, D Company, 5 RAR, was fired on with rifles and rocket-propelled grenades by an enemy squad. One Australian was killed and two wounded; two to four enemy were killed and four weapons captured. The platoon seems to have stayed in one place too long and been spotted.

2566.summary: 10 Platoon, D Company, 6 RAR, had been in ambush in thick bamboo beside a track through the Courtenay rubber plantation for two days when about 60 enemy, a carrying party with stretcher-bearers and escort, walked into it. The Claymores were fired with as many as possible in the killing ground, followed by three machine-guns; the enemy fired a few wild shots and fled. The sweep found 22 dead and captured weapons, grenades, medical supplies and documents. Five of the eleven Claymores failed from faulty detonators, but the machine-guns, cleaned daily, fired 500 rounds each without a stoppage.

2588.summary: A combined patrol of 10 Australians of 3 Platoon, A Company, 5 RAR, and 55 South Vietnamese soldiers, moving to a new ambush site, was attacked from all sides by a platoon of Viet Cong main-force troops. Poor radio contact delayed artillery until a spotter aircraft relayed the calls, and the enemy closed in to escape the shells, but two helicopter gunships fired within 25 metres of the patrol and the enemy withdrew. Seven South Vietnamese were wounded by rockets; two enemy were killed and possibly six more.

2633.summary: C Company, 5 RAR, found a bunker system on the south-east edge of the Long Hai Hills with anti-vehicle mines, a Claymore and a command-detonated shell. That night 7 Platoon set off an M16 mine, and another went off while the wounded were being moved; a third was found nearby. Three Australians were killed and fourteen wounded, one of them an engineer.

2692.summary: Following up an earlier contact, the forward section of 7 Platoon, C Company, 9 RAR, came under heavy rocket and rifle fire from about a platoon in a large bunker system. The forward scout was killed and eight men wounded, one of them trying to reach him, and the section lost its weapons as it was dragged clear. 9 Platoon's move round the flank eased the pressure; low cloud ruled out air strikes, but helicopter gunships were very effective, and artillery fired through the night. When the company attacked the next morning after heavy shelling, the enemy had gone, leaving blood trails.

2697.summary: While 3 Platoon, A Company, 6 RAR, was clearing a harbour position half a kilometre south-east of Hoi My, the platoon commander stepped out of the cleared area and set off an M16 mine. He was killed and 18 were wounded, one of them a sapper. 750 pounds of rice was found nearby.

2698.summary: While the scene of the earlier mine blast near Hoi My was being cleared, another M16 mine went off, killing one Australian and wounding five, among them the battalion's medical officer and its commanding officer.

2746.summary: Four armoured personnel carriers of 3 Troop, B Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, set an ambush near the beach, one of several in the area, and fired on 20 to 25 Viet Cong in the killing zone. Thirteen were killed, four wounded and one captured, with no Australian casualties. Weapons, documents and packs of food and supplies were captured.

2747.summary: 12 Platoon, D Company, 5 RAR, was in ambush in two half-platoon groups 70 metres apart when about 45 enemy moved north along the track through both. Both groups opened fire, and the enemy withdrew hastily without firing back, dragging away bodies and wounded under fire. Gunships, artillery and mortars covered the area, and the sweep at first light found seven dead and captured rifles, Claymores, food and documents. One Australian was slightly wounded by a grenade and stayed on duty.

2752.summary: Tanks of B Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, at Duc Thanh saw five enemy 100 metres away. A sweep with searchlights found lights, which were engaged with canister rounds and artillery.

2833.summary: A Company, 5 RAR's Assault Pioneer Platoon heard voices ahead and, with 3 Platoon, assaulted a bunker system after artillery fire behind it to cut off the enemy. They met very heavy rocket and rifle fire from the bunkers and flanks, and pulled back to a clearing to evacuate the wounded; as the medical helicopters arrived, the enemy closed in and fired mortars, rifles and rockets into the wounded, until helicopter gunships drove them back and the evacuation was moved. One Australian was killed and more than 30 wounded; nine enemy were recorded killed and 25 wounded. The company commander said the radio net had been chaotic with every supporting element on it.

2885.summary: The enemy got through the Regional Force bunkers into Dat Do and came up against a small mobile advisory team from B Company, 9 RAR, firing rocket-propelled grenades. The team fought back with a gunship aircraft overhead through the night, and tanks, carriers and a platoon were assembled to attack at dawn, but the enemy withdrew at first light. Three or four Australians were wounded; four Regional Force soldiers were killed and four wounded, and one enemy was killed.

3036.summary: A small team of 1 Field Squadron clearing a road block on Route 326, working with B Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, set off a mine or booby trap. One Australian was killed and one wounded.

3048.summary: A Company ambushed a large enemy group of 50 to 60. 1 Platoon let a leading party of five through, and 2 Platoon, 200 metres away, let the vanguard pass and sprang its ambush on the next group of about 20; artillery and a gunship aircraft then fired on the larger group behind. Three enemy were possibly killed and six wounded, and 100 pounds of rice was recovered.

3110.summary: The mine-clearing team of 1 Field Squadron set off an M16 mine 300 metres north of Phuoc Loi. Four Australians were wounded.

3121.summary: A patrol from 8 RAR was fired on with a single shot by an enemy soldier in green moving east, who withdrew towards Hoa Long. There were no Australian casualties, and enemy casualties were not known.

3278.summary: 10 Platoon, D Company, 8 RAR, came on 30 to 40 well-trained enemy in six bunkers, and an engineer was shot. With 11 Platoon's support the platoon assaulted, silenced one bunker and beat off a counter-attack in nearly three hours of fighting, with helicopter gunships and artillery in support; one Australian was shot dead and two wounded. Dusk ended the fight, and when the company returned with tanks the next day the enemy had gone, leaving one body.

3357.summary: The record gives no account of this SAS patrol's ambush beyond the patrol commander's name; seven enemy were recorded killed and two wounded.

3363.summary: A patrol of 10 Platoon, D Company, 8 RAR, was in ambush at a track junction near the Suoi Hoa Nuoc when the machine-gun sentry heard a radio playing and waited until it was in the killing area. Claymores, a machine-gun and grenade launchers were fired, and the killing ground was then searched with grenades in a set pattern. Eight enemy, one of them a woman, were killed and two wounded Viet Cong captured, with weapons and grenades. The patrol commander stressed keeping fire low, with interlocking arcs.

3511.summary: 8 Platoon, C Company, 5 RAR, and company headquarters were ambushing a main track when the rear machine-gunner saw enemy coming along a footpad behind them and opened fire. One enemy was killed and the others escaped. One Australian was wounded when a Claymore shorted and went off.

3516.summary: 9 Platoon, C Company, 8 RAR, was carried by tanks to within a kilometre of a carefully chosen ambush site and slipped in unseen while the tanks made a diversion, with engineers checking the site for mines and 15 Claymores laid along the track. It let the first of four enemy groups pass, and wiped out the second and third with its Claymores; the first and fourth counter-attacked. Running low on ammunition, the platoon was supported by mortars, artillery and helicopter gunships, and within 40 minutes the tanks of 1 Armoured Regiment came back, cleared the killing ground and stayed through the night. Three Australians were wounded; ten enemy were counted dead, and 22 drag marks were found.

3537.summary: C Company, 8 RAR, captured a Viet Cong who said 40 enemy were in a nearby bunker system protected by mines. The company attacked with carriers of B Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, and tanks of 1 Armoured Regiment; a carrier was destroyed by two rocket-propelled grenades, killing two Australians and wounding more. After air and artillery strikes a second assault led by the tanks went through the bunkers to a deep creek, but the system was also protected by an anti-tank minefield, and the force was ordered to withdraw, taking more casualties from enemy who had reoccupied the bunkers. Twelve enemy were killed, mostly by the tanks' canister and high-explosive rounds; one tank was hit eight times and kept fighting. The system was later hit by B-52 bombers.

3538.summary: A section of B Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment's carriers, on a jungle trail to an ambush position, was ambushed by a rocket team that hit the leading carrier twice, piercing the hull and wounding its crew. The carriers' fire drove the enemy off, and 5 Platoon, B Company, 8 RAR, swept the area and secured a landing zone for the wounded. Three Australians were wounded. The enemy had come from a bunker system not then known; three bodies found a week later were credited to this contact.

3544.summary: After C Company, 8 RAR's heavy fight that day, B Company was rushed by armoured personnel carrier into blocking positions. 4 Platoon had just dismounted when a section came under heavy rifle fire and rocket-propelled grenades; one carrier was holed and a tank hit. Sweeping forward, the platoon saw Claymore wires ten metres into the jungle and was pulled back. Eight Australians were wounded, all by rockets; six enemy were killed, three of whose bodies were found a week later.

3550.summary: A tank of A Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, struck a 20-pound shaped-charge anti-tank mine in the jungle near the Long Hai Hills. The tank was put out of action and two of its crew were wounded.

3555.summary: An observation post of 8 RAR's Anti-Tank Platoon saw two sampans, and an 81 mm mortar fired on one approaching the position. Only debris was found.

3576.summary: A Company, 8 RAR, set off what was probably an M16 mine in the south-east of the Long Hai Hills, killing one Australian and wounding two.

3584.summary: 1 Platoon, A Company, 8 RAR, was moving carefully to an ambush site in the heavily mined south-east of the Long Hai Hills, with engineers clearing the way. It had reached the site, and was gathered around platoon headquarters, when one of the engineers set off an M16 'jumping jack' mine. Seven or eight Australians were killed and thirteen wounded.

3590.summary: Elements of 6 RAR/NZ attacked a new base of about 50 bunkers that the D445 Battalion had been building for a week since 8 RAR drove it from the Minh Dam base in the Long Hai Hills. 3 Platoon, looking for the camp, saw a well-used track and a poncho, and both forward sections came under intense rocket, machine-gun and rifle fire, including heavy machine-guns. They pulled back 100 metres while artillery, mortars and helicopter gunships hit the area; nine Australians were wounded, and the enemy withdrew, leaving one dead and many blood trails. The commanders noted that dense undergrowth limited their rockets and grenade launchers, and that navigation errors made support fire less effective.

3609.summary: B Company, 8 RAR, found an old, rusty M16 mine in the jungle six kilometres south of Xuyen Moc. While it was being destroyed the platoon deployed into all-round defence to look at some old bunkers, and someone set off another. Two Australians were killed and six wounded.

3741.summary: Men of D and E Platoon were hit by a command-detonated device of unknown type while moving along a civilian track. A sweep found nothing. Three Australians were wounded.

3763.summary: An armoured personnel carrier of 3 Troop, B Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, carrying troops of 5 Platoon, B Company, 8 RAR, on a track off Route 23, hit a 40-pound anti-tank mine. The carrier was badly damaged; one crewman was killed and about ten of those aboard wounded, one of them an engineer.

3768.summary: Engineers of 1 Field Squadron and A Company, 6 RAR/NZ, set off an M16 mine on a bullock track into a clearing in the jungle seven kilometres south of Xuyen Moc, after at least four men had already walked over it. One Australian was killed and four wounded. The mine had been laid after 8 RAR left the area, beside a Viet Cong marker of a broken branch; the company commander warned that clearings likely to be used as landing zones, and the tracks into them, should be expected to be mined.

3770.summary: B Company, 7 RAR, fought a bunker system of 18 bunkers along the bank of the Song Rai. To let 5 Platoon break off and evacuate its wounded, a patrol from company headquarters went in to draw fire and took casualties, and then a section of 4 Platoon moved up to assault a line of bunkers so headquarters could get its own wounded out, all under intense rocket and rifle fire, with helicopter gunships firing 10 to 15 metres ahead of the troops. Everyone was brought out and an air strike hit the bunkers; tanks could not get through the jungle before dark, and by morning the enemy had gone. One Australian died of wounds and five were wounded; four enemy bodies were found later.

3797.summary: 1 Platoon, A Company, 6 RAR, made contact with an unknown number of enemy, with unknown results.

3815.summary: 3 Platoon, A Company, 8 RAR, on its way to an ambush position, met 40 to 50 Viet Cong armed with rifles, rockets, machine-guns and grenade launchers. The platoon formed a firm base, and the enemy attacked from both flanks, closing to within ten metres to recover their dead and wounded. After an hour 3 Troop, B Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, arrived, and ten minutes later the enemy broke contact. Six Australians were wounded by rockets and grenades; two enemy bodies were found, and intelligence later put the enemy dead at over 50.

3822.summary: An SAS patrol found a bunker and a hut and moved into the camp, where five enemy sat round a cooking fire. They saw the patrol and tried to get away; the patrol fired rifles and grenades, and a sweep found two bodies and a rifle. The patrol leader remarked that moving eleven men through the jungle was hard, especially with Vietnamese troops.

3869.summary: A spotter aircraft directed 1 Platoon, A Company, 7 RAR, and the reconnaissance platoon to an occupied bunker system 800 metres away, and they went in by armoured personnel carrier behind tanks of 1 Armoured Regiment. The infantry attacked both flanks and the tanks the centre, and took some bunkers, but met intense rocket and rifle fire; a rocket hit a machine-gun team, killing the gunner, and 1 Platoon pulled back 75 metres with its wounded. The reconnaissance platoon did not get the order to withdraw and fought on, and a carrier was hit and towed out. One Australian was killed and twelve wounded; five Viet Cong were killed and three captured.

3925.summary: 9 Platoon, C Company, 7 RAR, fired on an enemy soldier in the sandhills south-west of Phuoc Hai, who fled leaving a heavy blood trail. Following the trail at first light, the patrol set off an M16 mine that the enemy had laid where a follow-up was likely to go. Two Australians were killed, one died of wounds and one was wounded.

3926.summary: An SAS patrol of 1 SAS Squadron engaged three enemy who were following it, killing two and possibly the third. More enemy movement was heard, and old camps were found nearby.

3944.summary: A platoon of 8 RAR following a new track saw two enemy near a bunker and killed one; heavy fire from two bunkers then pinned the forward section. The enemy withdrew and reoccupied the bunkers, causing more casualties, which were evacuated under helicopter gunship cover while ammunition was flown in. After holding the enemy for an hour, the platoon pulled back 800 metres for artillery and to join tanks and carriers; the assault later that day met no resistance. One Australian was killed and three wounded.

4081.summary: As 2 Platoon relieved 1 Platoon, A Company, 2 RAR, in a bunker system taken the day before, the commanding officer was showing his South Vietnamese counterpart round with a protection party when a booby-trapped 155 mm shell went off. Two Australians were killed and three wounded; both commanding officers were among the wounded and lost legs.

4087.summary: 2 RAR's Anti-Tank Platoon set off a Chinese mine while examining an enemy camp. Seven Australians, a New Zealander and a South Vietnamese soldier were wounded.

4092.summary: 8 Platoon, C Company, 8 RAR, ambushing Route 2 near Hoa Long, watched 50 to 60 Viet Cong move carefully into the village and moved its ambush to catch them on their way out. They came back at about 3 am, less alert, carrying packs, and headed straight for one group, so the ambush was sprung early; Claymores and four machine-guns in crossfire killed or wounded the whole first group, and the second withdrew with the wounded. 1 Troop, B Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, came up quickly, drove off a counter-attack and ran down more of the enemy hiding in scrub. Nineteen Viet Cong were killed and six captured, with a large haul of weapons, food and supplies; one Australian was wounded.

4103.summary: A grader of 1 Field Regiment set off an M14 mine with its blade. There were no casualties.

4169.summary: 9 Platoon, C Company, 8 RAR, ambushed six Viet Cong moving along Route 2. The ambush was sprung with Claymores, three of which failed, and machine-guns, and kept up until illumination from a spotter aircraft and carrier support arrived. Four enemy were killed and one North Vietnamese soldier was wounded and captured.

4245.summary: 6 Platoon, B Company, 2 RAR/NZ, was in ambush in a rubber plantation covering the house of a known Viet Cong food supplier. Ten unarmed people who saw the ambush and ran were not fired on. Later, after torches were flashed at the house and a lantern put out, the platoon heard people creeping towards it for 40 minutes, and sprang the ambush when there was whispering right in front of the machine-gun. The enemy threw a grenade and fought on from the flank until armoured personnel carriers were heard coming. Two Australians were wounded; ten Viet Cong were killed, and a prisoner later said fourteen had died.

4265.summary: An ambush by B Company, 7 RAR, with a section of carriers of 1 Troop, B Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, held its fire until about 45 Viet Cong filled the killing ground before dawn, then fired all its Claymores and every weapon it had. The enemy fought back with rifles, machine-guns and rockets and tried again and again to recover their dead. There were no Australian casualties; 21 Viet Cong were killed and nine wounded, and a large haul of weapons, a radio and important documents was captured. The dead included the second in command of the D445 Battalion, its political officer and several of its junior leaders.

4284.summary: 6 Platoon, B Company, 7 RAR, heard about 15 enemy pass 20 metres away but let them go because the ambush was badly aligned, and re-sited it along the track. When about 20 more came the other way, it let seven into the killing zone and opened fire at five metres. A dying Viet Cong threw a grenade into the machine-gun pit, killing one Australian and wounding one. Five enemy, a food-carrying party of the Long Dat district force, were killed, with more blood trails, and packs and food were captured.

4332.summary: A bunker system found earlier was hit by artillery and air strikes and then assaulted and taken by 3 Platoon, V Company, 2 RAR. The enemy had left.

4335.summary: Fresh enemy tracks in the Binh Chau area led B Company, 7 RAR, to set an ambush. The sentry saw two armed enemy and shot both; one died at once, and the other got 200 metres before dying and was found in the follow-up. Two rifles were captured.

4349.summary: D Company, 3 RAR, was in a night harbour on the edge of a paddy field when 11 Platoon saw movement and opened fire with Claymores and machine-guns, then fired on about ten enemy trying to recover bodies. Enemy right on 10 Platoon's perimeter answered with heavy rifle fire and threw a satchel charge inside it, killing the platoon commander; another soldier was shot dead, and two were wounded. The enemy, signalling with tin whistles, attacked D and C Companies through the night, and helicopter gunships, artillery illumination and a tank's searchlight were used against them until they withdrew.

4406.summary: Half of 8 Platoon, C Company, 3 RAR, heard chopping, digging and a dog barking near a track, fired grenades at the sound, and swept forward into a bunker system. The platoon commander and a machine-gunner were wounded and the patrol pinned down by heavy fire, and it pulled back; the commander later died of wounds. With their smoke grenades used up, the patrol could not mark its position, so the helicopter gunships could not fire, and one gunship was hit and its co-pilot killed. The rest of the company, the assault pioneers in carriers and a troop of tanks converged, and the enemy, probably a stay-behind group, withdrew. The platoon commander was criticised for attacking without a reconnaissance.

4445.summary: 1 Platoon, A Company, 2 RAR/NZ, following a freshly used track, fired on five enemy ten metres ahead, and was soon attacked on three sides with machine-guns, mortars, rockets, grenades and satchel charges by the headquarters and a company of the D445 Battalion. Gunships had trouble telling friend from foe, and a spotter aircraft, a medical helicopter and two gunships were hit by ground fire. After two hours, with ammunition low, the platoon fought its way out, abandoning its packs and the wounded's weapons, and 3 RAR's assault pioneers drove off the enemy's pursuit. Nine Australians were wounded, two of whom died, one of them an RAAF crewman. The enemy recovered a machine-gun, rifles, 30 Claymores and explosives from the battlefield.

4463.summary: A mine-clearing tank of 1 Field Squadron set off a 60- to 80-pound mine in the jungle off Route 328, which badly damaged the tank. It could not be determined whether the mine was command- or pressure-detonated.

4495.summary: A 2 RAR/NZ vehicle travelling on Route 2 was fired on with two rounds from the west.

4525.summary: 5 Platoon, B Company, 3 RAR, found a bunker system held by the 3rd Battalion of the 33rd North Vietnamese Regiment, and after a night of artillery and mortar fire went in at dawn. It was met by rifle and heavy machine-gun fire from bunkers 15 metres away and pinned down for most of the day under repeated attacks by helicopter gunships and Cobras; the forward observer was killed, and a helicopter bringing ammunition was shot down, two of its crew dying. In the afternoon tanks of C Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, D Company and carriers of A Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, attacked the system and secured it. Three Australians were killed, two of them RAAF, and twelve wounded. The company commander reported that a marker balloon worked where smoke could not rise through the high canopy, and that several machine-guns failed.

4539.summary: Three armoured personnel carriers of A Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, carrying men of D and E Platoon, were patrolling a track when the leading driver stopped at an illumination canister he suspected was part of a mine. The enemy, of the 274th Regiment, opened fire, and a rocket-propelled grenade hit a pile of Claymore mines on the back of the last carrier, which exploded, killing its crew and five of D and E Platoon. Eight Australians were killed in all, and two wounded.

4609.summary: 7 Platoon, C Company, 4 RAR, was following a track from an empty bunker system when its forward section crossed a steep gully and saw a bunker; as the section commander went forward, an enemy came out and the fight began. The platoon came under rifle fire from the bunkers, Claymore mines fired from the trees and then rocket-propelled grenades, and after about an hour withdrew by fire and movement, with artillery keeping the enemy in their bunkers. Three Australians were wounded; at least three enemy were heard crying out from wounds. Many shells and grenades failed to go off in the soft ground, and two machine-guns broke down, but the rifle-fired grenades proved their worth.

4611.summary: D Company, 4 RAR/NZ, with tanks of C Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, was searching for the 274th Regiment's 1st Battalion. Just after the tanks had left, 10 Platoon came under rocket fire from a bunker, and fire from the system grew intense; 12 Platoon killed three enemy fleeing another bunker. A troop of tanks came back and, slowed at first by thick jungle and the need to find the infantry, pushed 100 metres ahead of them through the bunkers, firing main guns and machine-guns, and cleared the system with the infantry. One Australian was killed and four or five wounded; twelve enemy were killed.

4616.summary: A tank of 1 Troop, C Squadron, 1 Armoured Regiment, set off a 40-pound mine on a jungle track east of Cam My. The mine had probably been in place a long time, with a recently fitted pressure trigger. There were no casualties, but the tank's suspension and four road wheels were damaged.

4635.summary: An SAS patrol had stopped to make radio contact when its second in command heard movement by a creek and saw three Viet Cong following the patrol's tracks. He fired at five to seven metres, killing one, probably a platoon leader of an enemy rear-services unit; the others returned fire, and the patrol suppressed the area and moved forward. A rifle, a pack and documents were captured.

4638.summary: 7 Platoon, C Company, 3 RAR, made contact with two enemy, who withdrew. The sweep found their tracks, a sandal and a hat.

4652.summary: 12 Platoon, D Company, 4 RAR/NZ, leaving its night position, was fired on from a well-established bunker system of the 33rd North Vietnamese Regiment's 3rd Battalion; one Australian was killed at once. Through the morning artillery, gunships and aircraft attacked the system, bringing fire within 40 metres. In the afternoon the company assaulted, and the leading section was cut down by fire from the flanks 15 metres short of the bunkers; the company withdrew, leaving its dead, and while pulling back ran into a second bunker system, where it was pinned down until dark with artillery brought within 100 metres. Five Australians were killed and nine wounded; eighteen enemy were killed, half of them by air attack. With V Company, the company recovered its dead and equipment two days later.

4655.summary: 6 Platoon, B Company, 4 RAR/NZ, following a telephone wire, fired on an enemy soldier rolling it up and followed his tracks. A party looking for a night position then met enemy on three sides, and the main body was hit by rifle and 60 mm mortar fire, taking heavy casualties; 4 Platoon came up to join it, killing one enemy on the way. Artillery, helicopter teams and air strikes of napalm, bombs and rockets supported the company. Fifteen Australians were wounded, three staying on duty; the enemy were thought to be the headquarters and support weapons of the 33rd North Vietnamese Regiment, and two bunker complexes were found around the contact area.

4665.summary: Armoured personnel carriers of A Squadron, 3 Cavalry Regiment, fired on two enemy after a light was seen at the perimeter. The enemy fired one shot, and a sweep found nothing.

4668.summary: A vehicle from Duc Thanh carrying three members of the Australian Army Training Team was fired on. There were no casualties and no damage.

4669.summary: 5 Platoon, B Company, 4 RAR/NZ, was fired on by two or three enemy in green and black, who withdrew. There were no Australian casualties.

4679.summary: Two engineers of 1 Field Squadron were killed when an anti-lift device went off while they were laying M16 mines in the barrier minefield.

4694.summary: 1 Field Squadron was helping a South Vietnamese battalion repair the minefield between Dat Do and Phuoc Hai when a South Vietnamese soldier stepped on an M16 mine. He was killed; two Australians and four South Vietnamese were wounded.

4705.summary: Australian and US artillery fired on an enemy mortar position. The next morning more than 18 bodies were found, nine of which were credited to 1 ATF's artillery.

4710.summary: A sapper of 1 Field Squadron set off an M16 mine while laying it in the barrier minefield. Six were wounded, two of whom later died.

4717.summary: A standing patrol near 103 Field Battery heard noises to its south for 20 minutes. Believing it had been given away, the patrol leader moved it 150 metres north to the battery's outer wire; about half an hour later the enemy threw a grenade into the patrol.

4758.summary: About 40 to 50 enemy attacked local forces at Thai Thien, and 1 ATF's artillery fired in support. Fourteen Viet Cong were killed, and weapons and parts of an 82 mm mortar were captured.

4761.summary: Artillery fired on an enemy mortar position.

4781.summary: A patrol from 2 RAR saw 30 to 40 armed Viet Cong moving west in close formation along a track, carrying one wounded man on a stretcher. 106 and 108 Field Batteries fired on the area with unknown results.

4863.summary: 5 Platoon, B Company, 9 RAR, found 26 new, recently used bunkers. Three bodies of men killed by artillery were found buried in the area.

5485.summary: An aircraft saw many cooking fires around Thua Tich, and the artillery fired 25 rounds into the area.

5607.summary: 106 Field Battery fired on suspected enemy mortar positions.

5850.summary: A Company made contact with one enemy, who was killed.

5856.summary: D Company made contact with three enemy moving south, without result.

5911.summary: A patrol of 9 RAR heard about three Viet Cong moving to its west, and fired pre-arranged defensive fire on the area with unknown results.

10016.summary: 1 RAR's advance guard arrived at Bien Hoa, and the rest of the battalion followed by air and aboard HMAS Sydney over the next weeks. Its soldiers first went out on patrols and ambushes with the US 2/503rd Battalion, and by mid-June were patrolling on their own, with nothing to report; a troop of armoured personnel carriers of the Prince of Wales Light Horse joined it. Its first shots were fired by the mortar platoon on 25 June, and its first casualties came the next day, when a grenade went off by accident, killing three and wounding seven, with one American killed. The first wounded by enemy action was a Light Horse officer, hit by harassing fire on 28 June.

10070.summary: 12 Platoon, D Company, 1 RAR, clearing the ground for a battalion harbour, walked into open country covered by a Viet Cong ambush of four to seven men in well-built bunkers, who opened with grenades and automatic fire. Several men were wounded, including the platoon commander, and two medics were killed going forward to help them; a section sweeping to the east was pinned down, and a flanking attack by the company's support section met no opposition. Two Australians were killed and six wounded over an hour and twenty minutes. The lessons drawn were to avoid open ground and keep medics back until it was safe.

10079.summary: Engineers of 3 Field Troop pumped smoke and CS gas into tunnels found by B Company, 1 RAR, to reveal other entrances and deny them to the enemy. An engineer corporal inspecting a shaft was overcome by the gas and lack of air, and was dead when rescuers reached him; two of those who tried to reach him were evacuated. Documents, food, medical stores and a booby-trapped trapdoor were found in the tunnels and caches.

10144.summary: A Claymore mine went off in front of a small transport vehicle carrying rice out of a captured cache for B Company, 1 RAR, wounding two sappers of 3 Field Troop and an American soldier.

10185.summary: Operation 13/65, 1 RAR's search-and-destroy operation north-east of the US 173rd Airborne Brigade's base at Bien Hoa, with a troop of armoured personnel carriers, 3 Field Troop, and 105 Field Battery and New Zealand's 161 Battery in direct support.

10188.summary: 105 Field Battery fired a battery mission from Landing Zone Queen in support of the US 1/503rd Battalion, which had met a Viet Cong main-force unit north-west of the Dong Nai River. The airborne controller confirmed two Viet Cong killed.

10189.summary: The US 2/503rd Battalion was attacked from all sides of its perimeter for four hours, after a bombardment of mortars, a howitzer and recoilless rifles, probably by three battalions of the 271st Regiment. Artillery, including 105 Field Battery, and air strikes played a large part in defeating the attack. The Americans lost 7 killed and 114 wounded; 288 Viet Cong were counted dead. A large cache of weapons was found the next day.

10441.summary: C Company, 1 RAR, carried in the armoured personnel carriers of 1 APC Troop, Prince of Wales Light Horse, made a frontal assault along the road into the village of Vo Xu, with A Company in support and B and D Companies giving diversionary fire. It met light fire on entering the village and quickly secured its objective, the south-west of Vo Xu; two Viet Cong were thought to have escaped through tunnels.

10442.summary: 1 RAR moved into Vo Xu village with little trouble; 52 Viet Cong were captured and seven more gave themselves up. As B Company's cordon neared the south-east corner, 4 Platoon was fired on with machine-guns and rifles from across the La Nga River by an enemy group thought to be covering others escaping by boat. The platoon returned fire, and mortars, artillery and helicopters were used; about four enemy were thought killed, but no bodies were recovered. One Australian corporal was wounded and later died, and another soldier was wounded.
